specialty: novelty and positioning: is the contribution distinguishable from prior work, and is the novelty claim supported rather than asserted?
summary: The paper argues that a multiple-choice score should be tested against the construct's best constant, input-blind predictor (the gold-label-marginal 'floor') before any arm-to-arm comparison, and that this floor is itself an upward-biased estimator that needs its own calibration against a null the construct can realise. It reports nine letter-construct floors, four degrees of freedom that leave a content floor under-specified (tie convention, length unit, tokenizer, and the meaning of 'chance' under varying option count), a 17-cell MMLU-Pro read-out of structurally damaged arms, a 27-cell arm-conditional permutation re-analysis whose statistic is the numerator of Cohen's kappa stratified by option count, and an fp32-vs-bf16 control. Positioning is unusually explicit and mostly correct: majority-class baselines (Balepur et al.), length-normalisation pathologies (Oostermeijer), option-count-aware chance correction (Bennett, Brennan, Frary, Brenner, de Vries) and PriDe-style debiasing (Zheng et al.) are each attributed, and the claimed increment is narrowed to (i) the floor as a pre-comparison gate, (ii) the enumerated degrees of freedom, and (iii) the within-varying-k stratification. I verified the numbers extensively and they hold: every floor is exactly count/n (1403/12032, 3776/14042, 2033/3270, 138/500, 633/2376, 311/1172, 255/1221, 928/1838), the gaps and ratios recompute to the printed digits, the 36-item / 0.299 pp stratification footprint is 1439-1403 over 12032, 2051/12032 = 17.05%, E[m_J] = 9981/12032 x 0.1 = 0.082954, the binomial 0.0196 is 0.019568, shortgpt16's 5.2x is 3.674/0.702 = 5.231, my independent BH step-up over Table 7 reproduces all 27 q-values with 0 mismatches (six <= 0.05, five clear alpha/27), and the off-MMLU OLMo-2 slice reproduces from evidence/second_mc_benchmark/gate2_letter_content_nulls.csv as exactly 9 above floor (5 shortgpt16 + 4 keep14, smallest above-floor margin +6.47 vs largest at-or-below +2.61). The paper is also genuinely self-falsifying: the legality-aware null correction moves its flagship MMLU-Pro row from p<1e-5 to p=0.083, the abstract and introduction carry the weakened claim, and the two ARC rows that moved in the authors' favour are reported rather than absorbed. My concern is not honesty, it is what survives that honesty. After the corrections, the positive quantitative content reduces to two fixed-k constructs whose majority-class baselines are essentially a public-label computation, the statistical machinery is disclaimed as not new, the headline content-floor span is dominated by a convention the paper itself calls a reductio, and the flagship flip does not survive the multiplicity correction the paper reports about itself. Separately, two headline denominators and the fp32 tie counts are not checkable from the frozen artifact, the shipped emitter cannot run from the release, two named asserting gates are absent, the Reproducibility Statement describes a checker scope the shipped checker does not have, one table caption asserts an invariant its own row violates, and Limitations overflows onto page 10.
strengths: The positioning work is done, not gestured at. Section 2 (02_related.tex) separates the contribution from Balepur et al.'s majority-class baseline (their object is dataset cheatability under a generative setup; the operational contrast given is that their invalid-output analysis imputes 0.0 or 0.25 on MMLU while the best-constant letter value is 0.2689), from Zheng et al.'s adversarial 'null model' against judges, from PriDe (predictor-side vs reference-side), from OLMES's max-over-formulations rule, and from Oostermeijer's length-normalisation result. Appendix A.1 (09a_relocated.tex:8) then attributes the option-count-aware chance correction claim by claim to Bennett/Brennan/Frary/Brenner/de Vries and explicitly disclaims all of it. Section 3.2 (03_method.tex:36-49) states that Delta_perm is the numerator of Cohen's kappa and that the constant-emitter zero is the textbook kappa=0 property. This is the correct standard for a measurement paper and most submissions do not meet it.

The central self-falsification is real, load-bearing, and correctly propagated. Appendix A.1's legality-aware-null subsection (03b_nulls.tex:30-41) shows the paper's own calibration drew all 12032 MMLU-Pro gold letters uniformly over ten letters although 2051 items (17.05%) cannot have gold letter J, moving E[f-hat] from 0.104457 to 0.113873 and the flagship row from p<1e-5 to p=0.083. I confirmed against evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json that survives_aware = ['MMLU letter','BoolQ'] and that the abstract, introduction and Table 1 all carry 'only two of eight', not three. The evidence file additionally records that its own directionality contradicts an earlier verification record's asserted universal monotonicity, and the paper prints the two ARC rows that move in its favour rather than suppressing them. Very few papers report a correction that kills their largest construct.

Numerical provenance for the in-scope tables is strong and mechanically checkable. I recomputed all nine floors as exact rationals and all nine gaps/ratios from tab_nulls.tex and tab_construct_nulls.tex with no discrepancy; I independently reimplemented the monotone BH step-up over the 27 rows of tab_v2_full.tex and reproduced every published q_BH to 4 decimals with 0 mismatches, including that qwen3/k14 clears at q=0.0297 and olmo2/keep14 does not at q=0.0663, and that exactly five cells clear Bonferroni at 0.05/27 = 0.001852. The 5.2x half-width ratio, the 36-item/0.299 pp stratification gap, and the 0.0196 binomial all reproduce.

The prose-vs-evidence checker actually runs and passes on a clean copy of the release. I copied code/ and evidence/ into a fresh tree with the manuscript sections placed at paperC/sections/ and ran 'python3 code/check_prose_vs_evidence.py --out /tmp/rt/chk.json'; rc=0, verdict PASS, n_checked=65 n_ok=65 n_mismatch=0. Whatever it covers, it is not vapour.

The one-directional framing of the test is stated and defended rather than quietly assumed. Section 3.1 (03_method.tex:18) and the closing paragraph of Section 1 (01_introduction.tex:26) both say a floor pass certifies nothing, citing Feng et al.'s construction where a partial-input baseline sits at chance while artifacts remain exploitable. The paper is scrupulous about not overclaiming the direction of its own gate.

The exceptions to the aggregate are organised rather than tolerated, and the organisation is verifiable. Appendix A.6 (09a_relocated.tex:44) says all nine off-MMLU above-floor cells are OLMo-2 arms retaining at least 14 of 32 layers with no overlap against the at-or-below group; recomputing the letter x damaged x 5-task slice from the CSV gives exactly that partition (nine cells, +6.47 to +49.66, all shortgpt16 or keep14; the tenth keep14 cell, PIQA at +2.61, is correctly reported as at-floor). A test that failed indiscriminately would not place its rejections at one end of the ladder, and that observation is doing real work.
weaknesses: NOVELTY, CENTRAL. After the paper's own legality-aware correction, the surviving positive quantitative claim is that two fixed-k constructs have floors a balanced null could not produce: MMLU (0.268908 vs 0.25) and BoolQ (0.621713 vs 0.50) (tab_nulls.tex:11,17; 00_abstract.tex). But 02_related.tex:4 concedes that Balepur et al. already define a majority-class baseline for letter MCQA and recommend stronger-than-chance references, and 01_introduction.tex:3 concedes that Arcon et al. already report the above-chance/below-majority pattern. 'The majority-class baseline on MMLU and BoolQ exceeds nominal chance' is a computation over public gold labels. The three items the paper does claim are then each self-limited: the winner's-curse calibration returns a negative result on 6 of 8 rows (p = 0.083 to 0.853, and on CommonsenseQA and PIQA the floor is BELOW E[f-hat]); the varying-k stratification is described by the authors as 'a loophole-closing construction, not a new statistic' with measured footprint 36 items / 0.299 pp (09a_relocated.tex:8,15); and the content-floor degrees of freedom are attributed at the scoring level to Oostermeijer with only 'floor inheritance' claimed (02_related.tex:12). What remains distinguishable is a reporting recommendation (Appendix A.12 checklist) plus a case study. That is a real contribution but the delta over Balepur + Oostermeijer + the kappa literature is thin for a main-conference slot, and the paper's own candour is what makes the thinness visible.

NOVELTY/SCOPE. The headline size of the 'four under-specifications' is carried almost entirely by one convention the paper itself calls a reductio. Section 4's summary (03b_nulls_summary.tex:4) leads with a '40.6-point span' on MMLU-Pro, but recomputing from tab_conventions.tex with the 'credit' column excluded, the span is 6.998 pp on MMLU-Pro token, 15.6 pp on OpenBookQA token, and 15.358 pp on ARC-Challenge token; and on the default 'split' convention the entire length-unit effect is 0.45 pp (OpenBookQA 0.3635 vs 0.368), 0.98 pp (ARC-Challenge 0.274104 vs 0.283902) and 0.947 pp (Winogrande). Appendix A.1 concedes that 'a convention that lets an oracle harvest every tie is useful as a reductio, not as a neutral default' (03b_nulls.tex:12). So the number a practitioner actually faces is roughly 1 pp, not 40.6, and the headline should say which convention the span is a property of. The ARC-Challenge 'credit moves five of six arms from significantly above to significantly below' claim does check out in the CSV (6 above under split, 5 below under credit, base at floor), but it is again a statement about the reductio convention.

EVIDENCE COMPLETENESS. The abstract's off-MMLU headline, '9/85 cells above their floor against 45/85 above chance', is not reconstructible from the frozen artifact. The only off-MMLU evidence file, evidence/second_mc_benchmark/gate2_letter_content_nulls.{json,csv}, contains six arms and all six are OLMo-2 (7B_base, 7B_keep{8,10,12,14}, 7B_shortgpt16); grep for llama/qwen returns 0 hits in both files. The 60 non-OLMo off-MMLU cells that make up 85 - 25 therefore have no per-cell record here, and the strings '9/85', '45/85', '25/60', '7/60' and '0/60' appear nowhere in evidence/ or code/. I could reproduce only the 25-cell OLMo-2 slice (9 above floor, matching the nine named in 09a_relocated.tex:44). Given that Appendix A.5 (09a_relocated.tex:24) makes disclosed, checkable denominators the paper's own integrity standard, and that gate_designated_denominator.py is credited there with asserting exactly this cardinality, shipping a headline whose denominator the artifact cannot check is the same class of defect the paper says it repaired.

REPRODUCIBILITY CLAIM OVERSTATED, AND THE EMITTER DOES NOT RUN. 10_reproducibility.tex:3-10 states 'A checker walks all numerals in the source and requires each to be either an exact match to a value in the evidence set, a correct rounding of one, or a stated difference of two; at the time of writing it reports 610 numerals with none unresolved.' Running the shipped checker on a clean copy: rc=0 but n_targets=21, n_checked=65, n_skipped=12, n_uncovered=1 (the Winogrande control floor 0.504341 appears in no scanned file). By its own docstring it is not a walk over all numerals: MIN_DP=3 excludes any literal with fewer than three decimals, and its target set is 21 construct nulls. The figure 610 has no home in the release (the only match for that digit string in evidence/ or code/ is a line number in R7_BOOTSTRAP_P_FIX.md:62). Separately, the generated table cannot be regenerated: 'python3 code/emit_tab_construct_nulls.py' fails with FileNotFoundError on paperC/evidence/e2_single_source_assertion.json (required at emit_tab_construct_nulls.py:95, absent from the release), and it also requires paperC/sections/tab_nulls.tex at line 96. Two gates the manuscript credits with asserting its headline numbers, gate_designated_denominator.py (09a_relocated.tex:24) and gate_bh_27cell_consistency.py (tab_v2_full.tex:38, 'which reads this table as its only input'), are not in code/ at all. For a paper whose integrity story is that a drifted number becomes a build failure, the released build cannot fail.

INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY, VERIFIED. The Table 10 caption (tab_construct_nulls.tex:27) asserts: 'Where n_opt is constant the two nulls are the same distribution and the columns agree by construction, which is itself a check on the emitter.' PIQA has n_opt_is_constant = true (histogram {2: 1838}) yet the printed row gives blind 0.658 and legal 0.691 - a 0.033 disagreement on precisely the row where the caption says disagreement is impossible. The cause is in the evidence: p_aware = 0.691229 is evaluated at the exact rational floor 928/1838 while p_blind_shipped = 0.65791 uses the 6-dp stored floor, and p_aware_rounded_floor_convention = 0.657341 would agree. So the two columns differ along two axes (which null, and which floor convention), not the one the caption names; the same latent mismatch exists for MMLU and BoolQ but is masked by <1e-5. Appendix A.1's rounding paragraph (03b_nulls.tex:39) does disclose 'on PIQA 0.691 rather than 0.658', so the number is not hidden - but a caption that advertises an emitter self-check falsified in print by its own row is worse than no caption, and the caption never mentions the floor-convention axis.

STATISTICS. The abstract sells 'the flip is 3/12 above chance versus 1/12 above the floor' while Appendix A.4 (09a_relocated.tex:37) states that under BH at q=0.05 or Bonferroni NEITHER reference retains a single cell (0/12 both sides), so the corrected comparison is undefined. The fallback is a global-null binomial: 3-or-more rejections out of 12 has probability 0.0196 (I verified 0.019568). But that statistic does not support the contrast being advertised, because the floor side's 1/12 is also entirely consistent with the same global null: P(X >= 1 | n=12, p=0.05) = 0.4596. So the honest post-correction statement is 'the chance side is not uniformly null', which the appendix does say, and NOT 'the chance side rejects more often than the floor side', which is what 3/12 vs 1/12 in the abstract conveys. One of the paper's two headline flips therefore has no multiplicity-valid version, and the abstract should say so rather than leaving it to Appendix A.4.

BH FAMILY FRAGILITY, VERIFIED. Section 5.3 (05_analysis.tex:41) defends Table 7's BH as 'the one place in this paper where the family definition is not in dispute: one table, one null, one statistic, one item set.' It is more disputable than that. The paper itself notes (09a_relocated.tex:15) that five of the 27 cells are one Qwen3 healing run sampled 500 steps apart and two more are the same keep8 run at two steps. Collapsing the five near-duplicate heal cells to one leaves the verdicts intact (qwen3/k14 q=0.0253, olmo2/keep14 q=0.0565), which is reassuring and worth reporting. But restricting the family to the designated damaged arms - dropping the five intact anchors, which are not the subject of any tested claim and whose p=1e-4 values raise the step-up thresholds - gives qwen3/k14 q=0.0759 and nothing at all surviving. The single thing the paper says 'survives correction', and on which it rests the claim that v2 re-sorts rather than rescales, is therefore conditional on including five intact-model anchors in the multiplicity family. That dependency should be stated in the same sentence as the q=0.0297.

PRESENTATION, LIKELY HARD-CONSTRAINT VIOLATION. Limitations overflows onto page 10 of main.pdf. Extracting page 10, there are 24 non-blank body lines of Section 7 before the REFERENCES heading, running from 'One family at one depth cannot identify healing' through '...inaccessible from the audit network' - four full paragraphs. main.tex:37 places sections/07_limitations inside the main text, whereas the authors deliberately moved Ethics and Reproducibility after the bibliography with a comment citing the ICLR 2026 exclusion (main.tex:39-44), so they are aware of the rule; Limitations is not among the excluded sections. The authors should confirm against the author guide and cut or relocate, because a desk-check failure would be an avoidable way to lose an otherwise careful submission.

PRESENTATION. All 12 tables sit after the bibliography, on pages 14-26, while the text that discusses them is on pages 1-9: main-text page 2 refers to Table 1 on page 14, page 4 to Table 7 on page 20, page 7 to Table 5 on page 18. There are no figures. So a referee reading the 9-page main text sees zero tables and zero figures in line of sight, and Section 4 has been compressed to one 400-word block (03b_nulls_summary.tex) whose full development (Appendix A.1) is also past the references. This is legal but it makes the paper very hard to referee, and at least Table 1 (the nine construct nulls) and Table 5 (the 17-cell MMLU-Pro read-out) are the paper's primary evidence and belong in the main text even at the cost of prose.

CITATION HYGIENE. Not one dataset or model is cited. refs.bib has 17 entries and none is a dataset or model paper; MMLU, MMLU-Pro, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, OpenBookQA, CommonsenseQA, PIQA, BoolQ, Winogrande, OLMo-2-7B, Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, Qwen3-8B-Base and ShortGPT all appear in 04_experiments.tex:5,8 and throughout the tables with no citation. For a paper whose entire contribution concerns how benchmark scores should be reported, and which names 'shortgpt16' as an experimental arm, this is conspicuous and trivially fixable.

PROVENANCE. Section 5.4's fp32 numbers - 4,303 bf16 exact top-two ties, 2,532 changed letter argmax decisions, 18.03%, McNemar p=0.5702 - have no record in the release. Grepping for standalone 2532 and 4303 in evidence/ and code/ returns nothing (rc=1 both). E-E resolves to evidence/R7_BOOTSTRAP_P_FIX.md, which carries the bootstrap p-value repairs but not the tie or flip counts, and names the underlying records as '.../evidence/gate3_dtype_runs/*_dtype_summary.json', outside paperC and not shipped. The arithmetic is self-consistent (2532/14042 = 0.18032), and the fp32 result is one of the paper's cleaner negative controls, so it is worth making auditable: ship the six dtype summaries.
questions: Post-correction, what is the novel quantitative claim that a reader could not have obtained from Balepur et al.'s majority-class baseline plus one pass over MMLU and BoolQ gold labels? I am not asking rhetorically - if the answer is 'the winner's-curse calibration of the floor estimator', please say so in the abstract and lead with it, because that is the piece I could not find in the prior work you cite, and it is currently presented as a caveat on the floor rather than as a contribution.

Where are the 60 non-OLMo off-MMLU per-cell records? If they exist (the 25/60, 7/60 and 52/60 counts imply they were measured), shipping them closes the 9/85 and 45/85 denominators. If they do not exist in a per-cell form, the abstract should not lead with an 85-cell denominator.

Please restate the Reproducibility Statement to match what code/check_prose_vs_evidence.py does. What is the 610 figure, which artifact records it, and does it come from a tool that is in the release? As shipped the checker reports n_checked=65 over 21 targets with MIN_DP=3, which is a different and much narrower claim.

Will you ship evidence/e2_single_source_assertion.json, sections/tab_nulls.tex, gate_designated_denominator.py and gate_bh_27cell_consistency.py? Without the first two the generated table cannot be regenerated (I get FileNotFoundError), and without the last two the two headline assertions they are credited with are on trust.

Table 10's caption says the blind and legal columns agree by construction where n_opt is constant, but PIQA (constant, k=2) prints 0.658 vs 0.691 because the two columns use different floor conventions. Will you either evaluate both columns at the exact rational floor, or restate the caption to name both axes of difference?

For the 3/12-vs-1/12 flip: since neither reference retains a cell under BH or Bonferroni, and since 1/12 is also consistent with the global null (P(X>=1) = 0.46), what is the multiplicity-valid form of the claim that the chance reference is more permissive than the floor? If there is none, please move Appendix A.4's qualification into the abstract.

For the surviving v2 downgrade: qwen3/k14 has q_BH = 0.0297 over the 27-cell family, but q = 0.0759 if the family is restricted to the designated damaged arms (dropping the five intact anchors). Which family was pre-registered, and can the downgrade be stated with its family dependency attached?

Is Limitations excluded from the ICLR 2026 9-page main-text limit? You correctly moved Ethics and Reproducibility past the bibliography for that reason, but four paragraphs of Section 7 currently sit on page 10.

Would you consider one demonstration that the rule changes a conclusion in a paper that is not yours? The strongest possible version of this contribution is 'here is a published arm comparison that the floor test overturns'. Arcon et al. is cited as having noticed the pattern; a re-audit of one or two published MC comparisons under your protocol would convert a reporting recommendation into a result, and it needs no new training.
what_would_change_my_score: To 6 (no new experiments needed, all editorial/packaging): (1) ship the 60 non-OLMo off-MMLU per-cell records so 9/85 and 45/85 are checkable, or drop the 85-denominator from the abstract; (2) ship evidence/e2_single_source_assertion.json plus sections/tab_nulls.tex so emit_tab_construct_nulls.py runs, and ship gate_designated_denominator.py and gate_bh_27cell_consistency.py; (3) restate the Reproducibility Statement's '610 numerals' claim to match the shipped checker's actual scope (21 targets, 65 sites, MIN_DP=3), or ship the tool that produces 610; (4) fix Table 10's caption or evaluate both p columns at the exact rational floor, so the PIQA row stops falsifying the caption's stated invariant; (5) move Appendix A.4's 'neither reference retains a cell under BH' into the abstract alongside 3/12-vs-1/12, and state that 1/12 is also consistent with the global null; (6) attach the family dependency to the q=0.0297 downgrade (it becomes q=0.0759 without the five intact anchors); (7) resolve the page-10 Limitations overflow; (8) bring Tables 1 and 5 into the main text; (9) cite the datasets and models; (10) qualify the '40.6-point span' with the convention it is a property of, and give the ~1 pp default-convention figure alongside it. To 8 I would need new evidence, not new prose: either more fixed-k constructs whose floors clear the calibration (the current count is two, and the abstract's strongest quantitative claim rests entirely on them), or one worked re-audit showing the protocol overturns a comparison published by someone other than the authors. As it stands the paper's own corrections have left the reporting rule intact and the quantitative case thin, and I do not think prose can close that gap.
blindness_breach_observed: No breach that told me what to conclude. I saw no author notes, no target score, and no text instructing a verdict; the manuscript, code and evidence are all written as a submission. I did however find a process leak the authors should strip before submitting: code/recompute_legality_aware_nulls.py:6 and code/emit_tab_construct_nulls.py:27 both say 'Four of the six round_04 blind reviewers (X1/X2/X5/X6) independently flagged...', evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json:4 repeats it, and code/recompute_legality_aware_nulls.py:482 refers to 'a different round_04 defect'; evidence/mmlu_scale_power/mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json's DENOMINATOR_FIX_20260816 block cites 'round_04 R1-01'. These disclose that a prior internal review round existed, how many reviewers there were, and which of them raised which defect. That is provenance for a correction rather than steering, and it did not affect my judgment - I re-derived the correction from the evidence myself - but it is de-anonymising of the authors' workflow and does not belong in a released artifact.
